findings.title: No re-check of cache after acquiring write lock (thundering herd on cold start)
findings.body: After the RLock fast path misses, every concurrent caller takes the write Lock and independently re-reads the manifest from disk. In production mode (non-Dev) the cache only needs to be populated once, so callers that were queued behind the first writer should re-check `entryPointAssetsCache != nil` after `Lock()` and return it. As written, N concurrent requests at startup each redo the file read and JSON parse serially. In Dev mode every request serializes on the write lock, which is intended there, but in production this is redundant work.

findings.title: Cache is overwritten with nil/partial result when loading fails
findings.body: `entryPointAssetsCache = result` is assigned unconditionally, even when `err != nil` and `result` is nil. A transient failure (e.g. a Dev-mode reload hitting a half-written manifest) wipes a previously good cached value. The function also returns `(nil, err)`, so callers that ignore the error get a nil pointer. The cache should only be updated on success. This behavior existed before, but the new lock makes the write path explicit and it is worth fixing here.

findings.title: Returned pointer is shared and mutated in Dev mode without synchronization
findings.body: The lock only protects the pointer variable. The `*dtos.EntryPointAssets` it points to is handed out to many callers and is not guarded. In the non-Dev path the object is created and mutated (via `SetContentDeliveryURL`) before it is stored, so that is fine. However, the data race concern is only partially addressed: any caller that mutates the returned struct still races with other readers. No test (for example one run with `-race` and concurrent callers) was added to verify the fix.
